newsitem.title: USA: Integrated grows services with RoTech buy.
newsitem.headline: Integrated grows services with RoTech buy.

text.p: Integrated Health Services Inc will broaden its home-healthcare services and grow its per share income with the $615 million RoTech Medical Corp acquisition, a deal assembled after a similar pact with Coram Healthcare Corp unraveled last April.

"The transaction makes a lot of sense. Integrated has a big presence in the home-nursing business, but not in respiratory, intravenous therapy or durable medical equipment," said Morgan Stanley Dean Witter analyst D. Scott Mackesy.
"The (RoTech) acquisition is similar to the Coram acquisition. It brings in the respiratory therapy and intravenous business lines," he said.
"It makes sense to enter into those product lines to further service the HMO contracts the company has, so strategically I like the deal," added Mackesy, who rates Integrated a strong buy.
"RoTech is an excellent fit with IHS as we build our post-acute care network. It expands and broadens the services we are providing," Integrated executive vice president Marc Levin told Reuters.
The combined company would have total revenues of about $2.3 billion and home health revenues of more than $1 billion, the companies in an announcement.
Terms of the deal call for Integrated to issue 0.5806 share of common stock for each RoTech common share outstanding, and Integrated would assume about $300 million in RoTech debt.
In afternoon trade, Integrated shares fell 2-13/16, or 7.2 percent, to 36-1/8, while RoTech stock gained 1-3/8, or 7.3 percent, to 20-1/4.

Levin also noted other benefits of the transaction: immediate accretion to Integrated's per share earnings and the reduction of the company's debt-to-capital ratio. He declined to detail the expected impact on earnings.
The deal to close by the end of 1997, the companies said.
According to First Call, the analyst consensus forecast for Integrated's earnings for 1998, the period to be most affected by the deal, is $3.00 per share.
The 1997 view is $2.57 per share, up from $2.20 earned in 1996 before extraordinary and non-recurring items.
With the RoTech acquisition, debt-to-total-capitalization would be reduced to about 55 percent from 65 percent at March 31, 1997, Integrated said in the announcement.
Integrated "is a little bit overleveraged right now. Improving the balance sheet will be important for them to make acquisitions and grow going forward," the Mackesy said.
In April, Integrated Health said it terminated its merger pact with Coram, valued at $655 million, including debt assumption, when it was announced last October.
Levin declined to say why the deal was not consummated.
Integrated Health paid Coram $21 million in a settlement related to the merger termination.
